goal: boost small business in SoMa without slowing Bay Bridge traffic

options.title: Alleys plus Ellis and Sutter (Clementina, Minna, Ellis, Sutter)
options.rationale: This is the only plan that raises business revenue (+$128,246 in the model's revenue delta). It also cuts total delay by 122 hours and adds about 409 new social ties, with a total value of about $36.7M per year. The trade-offs are that 722 fewer commuters drive, 38 commuters are counted as 'gone', and rent pressure rises by 0.16. The model reports no Bay Bridge-specific figure, so total delay is the only traffic measure.

options.title: SoMa alleys: Clementina, Minna, Natoma
options.rationale: Total delay falls by 56 hours and 741 more commuters walk, for a total value of about $19.0M per year. Most of that value comes from mobility ($10.0M) and health ($8.6M). The economy pillar is negative (-$862K per year) and revenue falls by $18,634, so this plan does not help small businesses on the model's numbers. The model reports no Bay Bridge-specific figure.

options.title: Clementina + Minna only
options.rationale: This smallest option cuts total delay by about 98 hours and is worth about $18.1M per year, mostly from mobility and health. Revenue falls by $20,445 and the economy pillar is -$946K per year, so it does not meet the small-business goal and is the weakest of the three on that measure. The model reports no Bay Bridge-specific figure.
